text.more:
What is this?

This is an interactive map of relationships between Christian churches and denominations.

  • Each bubble represents a church or Christian denomination.
  • The colors represent broad traditions or communities of churches.
  • Each edge represents a relationship between two churches or denominations.
  • The strength of an edge represents the level of relationship between the two churches.
  • The layout was constructed using a force-directed graph algorithm, which places churches with stronger or more numerous connections closer together.


Relationship Levels

  • 100 — Full Communion: The churches recognize one another as fully united in the Church and share the highest level of ecclesial fellowship.
  • 25 — True Church: The churches recognize one another as true Christian churches, while not being in full communion with one another.
  • 5 — Cooperation: The churches recognize one another as fellow Christians and have a relationship of cooperation, without necessarily recognizing one another as being in full ecclesial communion.


Website Controls

  • Left click and drag to pan.
  • Scroll to zoom. The zoom in, zoom out, and center buttons at the bottom can also be used.
  • Click on a church to see its information and connections to other churches.
  • When a church is selected, the map is filtered to highlight its connections.
  • The right-hand panel displays information about the selected church, including its tradition, attributes, and related churches.


This project is an attempt to visualize the relationships between Christian churches and denominations in a single network. The classifications and relationships represented on the map are interpretive and may not reflect how every church understands itself or its relationship with other traditions.

This project was made with SigmaJS and Gephi.
